blocks.text: The build context is the file set the builder can read (usually the `.` in `docker build .`); anything not ignored can be COPY'd into layers and becomes part of the cache key.

items: Host `.venv`/`node_modules` (maybe macOS builds) overwrite the image's dependencies.
`.env` and credentials get baked into a pushable image.
Data, models, notebooks inflate build time and size.

blocks.code:
.git
**/__pycache__
.venv
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
data/
models/
notebooks/
tests/
Dockerfile*
compose*.yaml

items: Patterns are relative to the context root; `**` matches any depth; `!` re-includes (last match wins).

blocks.text:
$ docker build -f docker/api.Dockerfile -t rag-api .
$ docker build --build-context shared=../shared .   # then COPY --from=shared
COPY paths are relative to the context, never the Dockerfile. `COPY ../x` fails.
Watch the "transferring context" size. Hundreds of MB for a small API means the ignore file is wrong. With a remote DOCKER_HOST, the context also crosses the network.

Q: "Why does every commit trigger a full rebuild, and how do you stop secrets entering images?" A: "The context includes .git (or other churn) so COPY . . misses the cache; a strict .dockerignore excluding .git, .env, venvs and data fixes both the cache busting and the secret leak."

items: Named build contexts reach outside dirs safely.
